newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila says weaker peso will boost fiscal position.
newsitem.headline: Manila says weaker peso will boost fiscal position.

text.p: The Philippine Monetary Board's de facto devaluation of the peso would have a positive impact on the country's fiscal position, Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo said on Friday.

"For instance, a depreciation by a peso to $27.50 to a dollar is estimated to raise revenue collections of the Bureau of Customs by four billion pesos annually while expenditures will increase annually by only 600 million," De Ocampo said in a statement.
The net fiscal impact is 3.4 billion pesos annually, he said.
De Ocampo said a half-year impact implied that the projected surplus at the end of the year would rise to 8.8 billion pesos from 7.1 billion.
He said the decision to let the peso move in a wider range would also relieve pressure on the currency and allow the Central Bank to lower the overnight interest rate.
